contents.body_tr:
Türk savunma ve havacılık sanayisi, 2000’li yılların ortasından itibaren adını dünyaya duyurmaya başladı. Sektörün bu dönemde dünyada ses getiren ürünleri arasında, kompozit malzemeler kullanılarak inşa edilen yüksek süratli deniz platformları da önemli bir yere sahipti. Bu sayımızın kapak dosyasına konuk olan ARES Tersanesi de sektörün bu alandaki öncü firmaları arasında yer aldı.

Gemi inşa kabiliyetlerini ve faaliyet alanlarını sürekli genişleterek 20. yılına ulaşan ARES Tersanesi, firmanın Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Kerim Kalafatoğlu tarafından, yat inşa etmek amacıyla 2006 yılında kuruldu. ARES Tersanesi’ni kurmak için Trabzon’dan Antalya’ya gelen Kalafatoğlu, bir taraftan da askeri platformlar alanındaki gelişmeleri takip ediyordu. Kuruluşundan sonraki birkaç yıl sadece yat inşa eden firma, Kalafatoğlu’nun 2008 yılında verdiği cesur bir kararla kompozit malzemelerle askeri platform inşasına da soyundu. Bu alanda da başarılı olan ARES Tersanesi, özellikle ihracat projeleriyle adını duyurdu....

contents.title_tr: KalDer Ankara, 29. Kalite Çemberleri Paylaşım Konferansı'nda Sektörleri Buluşturacak
contents.summary_tr: Türkiye Kalite Derneği (KalDer) Ankara Şubesi tarafından düzenlenen 29. Kalite Çemberleri Paylaşım Konferansı, 18 Kasım'da Orta Doğu Teknik Üniversitesi (ODTÜ) Kültür ve Kongre Merkezi'nde gerçekleştirilecek. Türkiye'nin farklı…
contents.body_tr:
Bu yıl 29'uncusu düzenlenecek konferansta; tekstil, otomotiv, enerji ve gıda gibi farklı sektörlerden ekipler, geliştirdikleri iyileştirme projelerini katılımcılara sunacak. Etkinlik, kuruluşların birbirlerinin deneyimlerinden yararlanmasını, başarılı uygulamaların yaygınlaştırılmasını ve kurumlar arasında yeni iş birliklerinin geliştirilmesini amaçlıyor.

KalDer Ankara tarafından 29 yıldır düzenlenen konferans, kurum içi katılımcı yönetim anlayışının güçlendirilmesine ve çalışanların iyileştirme süreçlerine katılımının artırılmasına katkı sağlıyor. Farklı sektörlerden ekiplerin projelerini paylaşmasına olanak tanıyan organizasyon, kuruluşlara kendi kalite uygulamalarını diğer kurumlarla karşılaştırma fırsatı da sunuyor.

Konferans kapsamında, 2008 yılından bu yana verilen Kalite Çemberi Ödülleri ile 2011 yılından bu yana verilen Kaizen Ödülleri de sahiplerini bulacak. Ödüllendirme sürecinde, kuruluşlar tarafından hazırlanan başvuru raporları değerlendiriliyor ve gönüllü değerlendirme ekiplerince saha ziyaretleri gerçekleştiriliyor. Değerlendirmelerin sonuçları, konferans kapsamında düzenlenecek ödül töreninde açıklanacak.

Etkinliğe ilişkin ayrıntılı bilgiye ve kayıt bağlantısına https://ankara.kalder.org/ adresinden ulaşılabilirsiniz.

contents.body_tr:
Meeting the needs of naval forces with its advanced capabilities, MKE will highlight the DENIZHAN naval gun and the PIRANA kamikaze unmanned surface Vehicle (KUSV) at IDEF 2025. DENIZHAN was developed using MKE’s in-house engineering capabilities to meet the 76/62 naval gun requirements of the Turkish Naval Forces Command (TNFC), as well as those of allied and friendly countries.

Capable of performing surface warfare, air defence, and naval gunfire support missions, DENIZHAN stands out with features such as a high rate of fire, a low radar cross-section turret, and compatibility with modern combat management systems....

contents.summary_tr: Meteksan Defence offers Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) solutions that perform effectively in today’s operational environments, which are characterised by intense electronic warfare. The company’s AGNOSIS and SEDEN product…
contents.summary_en: Meteksan Defence
contents.body_tr:
Meteksan Defence offers Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) solutions that perform effectively in today’s operational environments, which are characterised by intense electronic warfare. The company’s AGNOSIS and SEDEN product families deliver reliable GNSS data to end users, while providing main contractors with platform-specific adaptability and a dependable supply chain. Various members of these product families are operational on approximately 60 different platform types in Türkiye and across the globe.

The GNSS product families developed by Meteksan Defence provide significant flexibility to users and platform integrators alike, thanks to their various configurations. The AGNOSIS family includes models both with and without an integrated GNSS receiver. The models without receivers deliver jam-resistant GNSS signals through antenna arrays of 4, 8, or 16 elements, and can be used alongside a wide range of GNSS receivers. These configurations are typically chosen for platforms already equipped with a GNSS receiver.

The models of AGNOSIS that include an integrated GNSS receiver present a complete, end-to-end solution. These models feature the same receiver hardware used in the SEDEN product family and deliver accurate and dependable positioning and timing information that is resistant to both spoofing and jamming. Their integrated GNSS hardware allows for a smaller system footprint compared to setups where this hardware exists as a separate unit, offering a key advantage in platform integration....

contents.body_tr:
Logos, which develops high‑pressure pneumatic system solutions for the defence and aerospace industry, is highlighting its high‑pressure vessel system product line at IDEF this year. Highlighting the company’s innovative work, in 2024, Logos received the High‑Tech Development Award from Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of Defence Industries. With strong infrastructure investments made at the start of 2025, the company aims to strengthen its position as a turnkey provider of advanced technology systems with fully integrated solution competence.

End‑to‑End Expertise in High‑Pressure Vessel Systems

Logos offers an integrated systems approach that maintains control and quality throughout the entire production cycle—not just for the final product. Manufactured from stainless steel and titanium alloys, these cylinders are filled with various gases such as nitrogen, air, and argon at pressures up to 700 bar for use in numerous critical applications....

The company has successfully completed over 200 projects to date, delivering solutions using the latest technologies and methodologies in areas ranging from desktop applications to web and mobile platforms, embedded software solutions to mission-critical systems, as well as independent testing and test automation.

contents.summary_tr: Powering Naval Superiority: Dependable, Clean Power Solutions from NOVA Power
contents.summary_en: Powering Naval Superiority: Dependable, Clean Power Solutions from NOVA Power
contents.body_tr:
Modern naval vessels are increasingly equipped with advanced, power-hungry mission systems. As warships evolve into complex network centric command centres, their onboard electrical infrastructure comes under increasing stress. NOVA Power Solutions (NOVA Power) delivers advanced power conditioning solutions that directly address the risks posed by these evolving demands, supporting navies worldwide.

At the core of these challenges lies a silent but serious issue: harmonic distortion in shipboard power systems. To maintain operational readiness and extend mission endurance, and protect vital electronics, navies must address this hidden threat. Harmonic mitigation not only enhances system reliability but also improves fuel efficiency, reduces energy losses, and extends the life of expensive onboard systems.

Süleyman Bayramoğlu, International Business Development Manager at NOVA Power Solutions: “Modern naval ships are digitally integrated, networked systems afloat, built around power-sensitive technologies that require consistent, conditioned, and continuous power to operate reliably under all conditions.”...

contents.summary_tr: Karel’s Defence Solutions: Indigenous Engineering and Production Strength for Global Markets
contents.summary_en: Karel’s Defence Solutions: Indigenous Engineering and Production Strength for Global Markets
contents.body_tr:
With nearly four decades of engineering experience and robust production capabilities, Karel remains a trusted partner in the technological transformation of the defence and aerospace industry. Having grown in Türkiye and offering technology solutions to global markets, the company provides integrated solutions for its stakeholders. More than just a supplier of communications solutions for the defence and aerospace sectors, Karel operates as a full-fledged technology company delivering turnkey solutions across the entire value chain —from design and production to testing processes and system integration.

In addition to defence industry, Karel operates in four distinct domains: Communication Systems, Corporate Projects, Automotive Technologies, and Electronic Production technologies. In each of these domains, the company designs, develops, manufactures, and operates products and solutions tailored to specific customer needs.

Leveraging its extensive expertise in communication systems developed for both civil and public sectors, Karel equips the communication infrastructures of land, sea, and air platforms with the state-of-the-art technologies. Its hybrid communication and control systems, supporting analogue, digital, and IP users, enable continuous and secure communication under challenging environmental and operational field conditions. Radio link systems ensure uninterrupted transmission of data, voice, and video over long distances. Spanning a wide range of products from switches and gateways to in-vehicle systems and shipboard alarm and announcement systems, Karel’s portfolio embodies high field performance, centralised management capabilities, and future-ready flexibility. All these systems are developed using Karel’s proprietary engineering and indigenously developed software....

The company’s products are also on top of the competition in the international markets, as BMS DEFENCE ranked on the third place in the highest exporters list of Turkish defence and aerospace industry with its 2024 export figures.

contents.title_tr: Alican ÖKÇÜN, Chairman of the Board at Nero Industries: (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Alican ÖKÇÜN, Chairman of the Board at Nero Industries:
contents.summary_tr: “Under the umbrella of Nero Group, we have laid the foundation for a robust structure that supports those in need of our solutions today and will continue to stand by them in the future.”
contents.summary_en: “Under the umbrella of Nero Group, we have laid the foundation for a robust structure that supports those in need of our solutions today and will continue to stand by them in the future.”
contents.body_tr:
At the heart of the Nero Group, Nero Industries has been playing active role in Türkiye’s defence and aerospace sector for 16 years. As the company evolved in parallel with the sector, this growth led to the establishment of multiple group companies operating in complementary fields. This process, which began in 2017 and gained momentum in recent years, resulted in the formation of the Nero Group, now comprising 15 companies. With a focus on technology and innovation, Nero Group companies offer distinctive products and solutions both in Türkiye and abroad. The group’s long-term strategy is centred on remaining as a trusted solution partner for its stakeholders while maintaining a sustainable and continuously evolving business model. Alican Ökçün, Chairman of the Board at Nero Industries, shared with the readers of MSI TDR Magazine the story behind the group’s formation, its strategic direction, activities, and future objectives.

 

MSI TDR Magazine: Mr. Ökçün, since 2009, Nero Industries has been operating in the defence and aerospace sector as a subsystem manufacturer. Over the years, we have observed a continuous expansion of your product portfolio, along with the establishment of new companies. Today, this structure has evolved into a corporate group under the umbrella of Nero Group. Could you outline the key stages in the transformation from Nero Industries to Nero Group?...

contents.title_tr: Five Companies from the Turkish Defence and Aerospace Industry Among the World’s Top Defence Companies (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Five Companies from the Turkish Defence and Aerospace Industry Among the World’s Top Defence Companies
contents.summary_tr: The US-based Defense News magazine has released this year’s edition of its “Top 100” list, which ranks the world’s leading defence and aerospace companies. Based on the total revenues of global firms, the list includes ASELSAN, Military…
contents.body_tr:
The US-based Defense News magazine has released this year’s edition of its “Top 100” list, which ranks the world’s leading defence and aerospace companies. Based on the total revenues of global firms, the list includes ASELSAN, Military Factory and Shipyard Management Inc. (ASFAT), Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE), Roketsan, and Turkish Aerospace.

ASELSAN was the highest-ranked Turkish company on the “Top 100” list, placing 43rd after dropping one position compared to the previous year. Turkish Aerospace moved up from 50th to 47th place. Roketsan maintained its position, ranking 71st once again this year. ASFAT made a significant leap, rising from 94th to 78th. MKE also advanced in the rankings, climbing from 84th to 80th place.

Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of the Defence Industries, made a statement on September 2 regarding the list. Emphasising that the Turkish defence and aerospace industry continues to strengthen its position on the global stage, Prof. Dr. Görgün said: “This success reflects the determination of our engineers, the synergy within our sector, and the trust of our nation. Our sustainable growth strategy is not only a guarantee of today’s achievements but also a pledge for tomorrow’s global leadership. The Turkish defence industry will continue to rise with its strong outlook, innovative vision, and unwavering commitment to full independence. I wholeheartedly congratulate the companies, their executives, and all personnel in the field who contributed to this remarkable achievement.”

contents.title_tr: MKE Bids to Establish a 155 mm Ammunition Production Line in Poland (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: MKE Bids to Establish a 155 mm Ammunition Production Line in Poland
contents.summary_tr: Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) participated in MSPO 2025, held in Kielce, Poland, between September 2 and 5. During the event, which was also attended by Deputy Minister of National Defence Bilal Durdalı, the company engaged in…
contents.body_tr:
Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) participated in MSPO 2025, held in Kielce, Poland, between September 2 and 5. During the event, which was also attended by Deputy Minister of National Defence Bilal Durdalı, the company engaged in cooperation discussions aimed at reinforcing its global presence. One of the most prominent agenda items at MSPO 2025 was MKE’s proposal to establish a “155 mm Howitzer Ammunition Production Line” in Poland. Speaking to the press during the exhibition, Tolga Çelik, Deputy General Manager at MKE, stated that the decision-making process regarding the production line had reached its final stage and that MKE had been shortlisted with its proposal. Çelik also expressed the company’s readiness to cooperate in building the production capacity Poland requires.

 

MKE to Export 20 mm Ammunition to Poland

Following MSPO, the next stop for MKE was the DSEI 2025 exhibition in London. At this event, Poland once again took centre stage in MKE’s agenda. During the exhibition, MKE representatives held talks with officials from 43 different countries to explore potential areas of cooperation. One of the key outcomes was the conclusion of a major agreement with the Polish Air Force. Under the agreement signed at DSEI 2025, MKE will supply 20 mm ammunition for use in the cannons of Poland’s FA-50GF Fighting Eagle Block 10 light combat aircraft. In addition to this agreement with Poland, MKE representatives also signed two separate export contracts during the exhibition.

 

MKE Advances Both in Exports and Strategic Investments

MKE, which currently exports to 105 countries, is expanding its global footprint through key systems such as BORAN, the first howitzer export in the history of the Republic, and DENİZHAN, the 76/62 mm Indigenous Naval Gun. In 2024, MKE sustained its international growth with a turnover exceeding $1.2 billion.

Alongside its export achievements, MKE is progressing with large-scale domestic investments. The company is continuing work on the energetic materials plant, a project covering 4.7 million square metres. This facility ranks as the largest investment in the defence and aerospace sector and the third largest across all industries in Türkiye. In parallel, capacity expansion and new production line installations are under way at 10 factories and three facilities. Efforts have also accelerated to convert a defunct sugar factory in the Çarşamba district of Samsun into a nitroguanidine production facility. This initiative aims to meet national requirements while contributing to the local economy and social development.

A total of 323 investment projects is scheduled for implementation in 2025, with a combined value of $818 million.

contents.title_tr: Bayraktar TB3 In Service for the Turkish Land Forces (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Bayraktar TB3 In Service for the Turkish Land Forces
contents.summary_tr: The Bayraktar TB3 armed unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV) has officially entered the inventory of the Turkish Land Forces Command. With this delivery, the Bayraktar TB3 has, for the first time, been formally fielded by a branch of…
contents.body_tr:
The Bayraktar TB3 armed unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV) has officially entered the inventory of the Turkish Land Forces Command. With this delivery, the Bayraktar TB3 has, for the first time, been formally fielded by a branch of the Turkish Armed Forces.

Sources from the Ministry of National Defence announced during a press briefing held on September 4 that the inspection and acceptance procedures for the TB3s had been completed and that the systems had been added to the inventory of the Turkish Land Forces Command. Developed by Baykar, the Bayraktar TB3 is distinguished by its foldable wing configuration and its ability to take off from and land on short runways.

contents.title_tr: SARSILMAZ ACADEMY Highlights the Principles of “Safe and Effective Shooting” (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: SARSILMAZ ACADEMY Highlights the Principles of “Safe and Effective Shooting”
contents.summary_tr: The workshop on pistol basics, organised by SARSILMAZ ACADEMY, was hosted by Poligon ARER, located in the Gebze district of Kocaeli. Held on August 9, the event provided participants with insights from SARSILMAZ’s team of experts on the…
contents.body_tr:
The workshop on pistol basics, organised by SARSILMAZ ACADEMY, was hosted by Poligon ARER, located in the Gebze district of Kocaeli. Held on August 9, the event provided participants with insights from SARSILMAZ’s team of experts on the fundamentals of safe and effective shooting.

The event had limited registration slots and various types of firearms and ammunition were introduced, while topics such as trigger control, aiming, and post-firing safety were addressed. The workshop included both theoretical and practical sessions, and participants were awarded certificates upon completion. SARSILMAZ officials announced that similar workshops, as well as those in different categories, will continue to be held in the coming period.

Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) received an award for its human resources practices as part of the 10th edition of the Stevie Awards for Great Employers. MKE received the Gold Stevie Award in the Most Innovative Talent Acquisition Program category with its project "Spark" Young Talent Attraction Program. The company was also granted the Silver Stevie Award in the Achievement in Leadership Development category for its initiative Future Leader Development Program.

The Bronze Stevie Awards granted to MKE were presented for the following projects:

● Future Leader Development Program in the Achievement in Succession and Career Management category

● Future Leader Development Program in the Achievement in Leadership Development category

● Leadership Development Program 'Move' in the Best Use of Blended Learning category

contents.title_tr: NMS UK’s Dragon 4x4 Conducts Live-Firing with VENOM LR (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: NMS UK’s Dragon 4x4 Conducts Live-Firing with VENOM LR
contents.summary_tr: Dragon 4x4 vehicle produced by NMS UK, a UK-based subsidiary of Nurol Makina, took stage at the Close Combat Symposium (CCS) 2025, held in the United Kingdom from July 1-3. During the event, SYS Group company AEI Systems’ 30x113 mm…
contents.body_tr:
Dragon 4x4 vehicle produced by NMS UK, a UK-based subsidiary of Nurol Makina, took stage at the Close Combat Symposium (CCS) 2025, held in the United Kingdom from July 1-3. During the event, SYS Group company AEI Systems’ 30x113 mm VENOM LR cannon, integrated into another SYS Group company, UNIROBOTICS’s TRAKON 30 remote controlled weapon station (RCWS), underwent a live-firing test on a Dragon 4x4. The test demonstrated the system’s full compatibility with the M788 ammunition manufactured by General Dynamics and currently in service with the UK Armed Forces.

CCS 2025 brought together procurement authorities from the United Kingdom Ministry of Defence (UK MOD), delegations from NATO and partner countries, research institutes, and system integrators.

contents.title_en: DataBoss Competes on a Global Scale in Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Technologies
contents.summary_tr: Ongoing wars and conflicts around the world clearly illustrate how rapidly technology is transforming the modern battlefield.
contents.summary_en: Ongoing wars and conflicts around the world clearly illustrate how rapidly technology is transforming the modern battlefield.
contents.body_tr:
Ongoing wars and conflicts around the world clearly illustrate how rapidly technology is transforming the modern battlefield. Among the technologies driving this transformation, artificial intelligence and big data play a significant role.

The Turkish defence and aerospace industry, which has made significant strides in areas such as main platforms and munitions, is now demonstrating similar progress in the fields of artificial intelligence and big data. DataBoss, featured in the MSI TDR’s Turkish edition’s cover story, plays a pivotal role in enabling Türkiye to compete globally in these two emerging domains.

Prof. Dr. S. Serdar Kozat, General Manager of DataBoss, explains the company’s position in this competitive field with the following words: “As someone who closely follows both the academic literature and the global developments in the private sector, I can confidently say this: Whatever the most up-to-date technologies are around the world, we are working on those as well. Of course, there may be differences in scale. However, in terms of technology and capabilities, there is nothing we are lagging behind on. In fact, we can see that we are ahead of Europe. And I can confidently state that we are on par with the work being done in the United States—and even competing with them in certain areas.”...

contents.title_tr: CTech’s 20-Year Journey: From a Start-Up to a Global Brand (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: CTech’s 20-Year Journey: From a Start-Up to a Global Brand
contents.summary_tr: One of the companies established during the initial period following 2004, a year marked by key decisions that shaped the future of Türkiye’s defence and aerospace industry, was CTech.
contents.summary_en: One of the companies established during the initial period following 2004, a year marked by key decisions that shaped the future of Türkiye’s defence and aerospace industry, was CTech.
contents.body_tr:
One of the companies established during the initial period following 2004, a year marked by key decisions that shaped the future of Türkiye’s defence and aerospace industry, was CTech. Now celebrating its 20th anniversary, CTech was founded in 2005 as a venture capital company, based on an idea conceived in 2003.

As in many other cases, the Undersecretariat for Defence Industries (SSM), which became today’s Secretariat of Defence Industries (SSB), played a significant role in the establishment of CTech. The company was among the firms commissioned within the scope of initiatives aimed at developing the sector and integrating Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) into the defence ecosystem. Dr Cüneyd Fırat, General Manager of CTech and the guest of Turkish edition of MSI TDR’s cover story, described those early days as follows: “We had many ideas in mind when we founded CTech, but we did not have a specific initial project. In the early 2000s, the institution then known as the Undersecretariat for Defence Industries (SSM) had launched an initiative focused on SMEs. There were efforts to encourage the integration of SMEs into the sector. After submitting the necessary applications, we started to receive specifications both from SSM and from main contractors. One of the proposals we prepared in response to these specifications was accepted, and we signed our first contract before the end of 2005.”

In the years that followed, CTech took part in projects across a range of fields, particularly in modelling and simulation, communication systems, and cyber security. Although it was not apparent at the time, this initial contract would later prove to be of critical importance for the company's future. The project in which CTech developed the AYSEK modem laid the groundwork for the SecureARX modems, which are now also used by NATO....

contents.title_tr: KEYVAN Aviation Meets Aviation Data Requirements of Türkiye and Rest of the World (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: KEYVAN Aviation Meets Aviation Data Requirements of Türkiye and Rest of the World
contents.summary_tr: The Turkish defence and aerospace industry has recently designed and manufactured numerous major platforms using indigenous capabilities. Many of these platforms have entered into service with domestic users, while also being exported…
contents.body_tr:
The Turkish defence and aerospace industry has recently designed and manufactured numerous major platforms using indigenous capabilities. Many of these platforms have entered into service with domestic users, while also being exported to foreign markets. Especially for airborne platforms, the accuracy and timeliness of aviation data are critical to mission success.

In cover file of the Turkish edition of MSI TDR, we talked to Mehmet Keyvan, the Founder and Chairman of KEYVAN Aviation. Keyvan explained the critical role of data in aviation, and stated: “Data plays a vital role in aviation, as it is the key to both safety and operational efficiency. Without access to current and reliable data, flight safety can be compromised. Aircraft rely on this data for autopilot functions, as well as for take-off and landing. Moreover, outdated or inaccurate data can lead to inefficient operations, requiring more resources than necessary to complete a flight that would otherwise be completed using fewer.”

The strategic importance of indigenous aviation data becomes even more obvious in military applications. According to Keyvan, in the field of defence and security, it is not only the aviation platforms and systems that should be developed domestically, but also the data they rely on: “When you obtain data from external sources, you risk revealing operational insights such as your intended destinations or mission routes, depending on the type of data obtained. This introduces potential security vulnerabilities. Accurate and up-to-date data is just as critical for military and security aviation operations as it is for civilian aviation. From this perspective, the origin of aviation data gains even greater significance in defence and security applications.”...

contents.title_tr: BEST DEFENCE Brings Its RCWS Expertise to the Naval Platforms (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: BEST DEFENCE Brings Its RCWS Expertise to the Naval Platforms
contents.summary_tr: One of the important collaborations in the Turkish defence and aerospace sector took place last year between SARSILMAZ and Best Group, resulting in the establishment of BEST DEFENCE.
contents.summary_en: One of the important collaborations in the Turkish defence and aerospace sector took place last year between SARSILMAZ and Best Group, resulting in the establishment of BEST DEFENCE.
contents.body_tr:
One of the important collaborations in the Turkish defence and aerospace sector took place last year between SARSILMAZ and Best Group, resulting in the establishment of BEST DEFENCE. With the founding of BEST DEFENCE, SARSILMAZ gained a significant advantage in the field of remote-controlled weapon systems (RCWS), by offering the turret, weapon and ammunition from a single source.                    

Established as a result of SARSILMAZ’s strategic move towards becoming a technology company focused on the defence industry, BEST DEFENCE has rapidly progressed since its inception. Drawing strength from its well-established legacy, the company initially focused on delivering RCWS solutions primarily for land platforms. This product range has now been expanded with the addition of the naval-type RCWS product family, which is the subject of this issue’s special coverage. As a result, the advanced capabilities once offered to land systems are now also available to naval platforms. These include support for weapons of various calibres, AI-assisted target detection and tracking, high-precision engagement, and the ability to procure the turret, weapon, and ammunition as a one-stop solution from a single source.            

Aziz Karaş, General Manager of BEST DEFENCE, outlined their objectives for the naval-type RCWS product family as follows: “We aim to replicate the success we have achieved with our RCWSs on land platforms in the naval platforms. For naval platforms, we provide best-in-class RCWS solutions. Our products are highly appreciated by end users for their ease of use and operational flexibility. The ability to deliver the RCWS together with the weapons and ammunition supplied by our group companies plays a key role in procurement authorities choosing us. We take pride in the fact that no other player offers solutions at this level of integration in the global market.”...

contents.title_en: IDEF 2025 SPECIAL ISSUE / SSB Message
contents.summary_tr: Today, Türkiye’s defence industry, comprising main contractors, subcontractors, SMEs, research institutions, and universities, has evolved into one of the country’s most vital sectors. As a result of the efforts we have carried out in…
contents.body_tr:
Today, Türkiye’s defence industry, comprising main contractors, subcontractors, SMEs, research institutions, and universities, has evolved into one of the country’s most vital sectors. As a result of the efforts we have carried out in the areas of defence system procurement and strategic guidance of the industry, our defence products and services are successfully delivered both to our heroic security forces and to the armed forces of friendly and allied countries with whom we have strategic partnerships across different geographies.

Our indigenous and national products are actively used in counter-terrorism operations and military missions both at home and abroad. contents.body_tr:
ANDAR, a company that is focused on the design and production of electromechanical actuators, is

Serkan Kale, Reşat Hakan Avcı, and Gökhan Koyuncu, the founding partners of ANDAR, state this current period as the “period of mastery” for the company, with the company planning to stand out as a manufacturer as well as a designer. In this direction, could you first explain the concept of this new factory and why you needed such a concept?...

contents.title_tr: MENATEK’s 30-Year Journey: From a Small Apartment Unit to Becoming a Leading Exporter (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: MENATEK’s 30-Year Journey: From a Small Apartment Unit to Becoming a Leading Exporter
contents.summary_tr: MENATEK was established exactly 30 years ago by the late Kazım Ünal to supply spare parts to the Turkish Armed Forces. A significant shift in the company's trajectory occurred in 2000, when it began providing spare parts for NATO. The…
contents.body_tr:
MENATEK was established exactly 30 years ago by the late Kazım Ünal to supply spare parts to the Turkish Armed Forces. A significant shift in the company's trajectory occurred in 2000, when it began providing spare parts for NATO. The company’s export activities, initiated through NATO projects, soon expanded to include the United States.

Between 2002 and 2005, MENATEK operated as a subcontractor for the main contractors of the United States Army, exporting domestically manufactured land vehicle spare parts from Türkiye to the US. In 2006, the company’s executives initiated the administrative procedures that would enable MENATEK to sell directly to the US Army. By 2007, the firm had secured its first contract from the United States. Around the same time, MENATEK also began shipments to Germany and Spain.

What began as a one-person operation in 1995 has grown into a team of 80, with MENATEK now possessing the capability to manufacture all mechanical subsystems of tracked vehicles. The company’s product range encompasses components for all major subsystems, including weapon systems, running gear, braking systems, heating and cooling systems, lubrication systems, and power transmission systems....

contents.title_tr: Platform Exports Fuels Turkish Defence and Aerospace Industry at IDEF 2025 (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Platform Exports Fuels Turkish Defence and Aerospace Industry at IDEF 2025
contents.summary_tr: The 17th edition of the IDEF once again demonstrated that the Turkish defence and aerospace industry has reached a globally competitive level. Reflecting the industry’s current standing, this year’s event was marked by major contracts…
contents.body_tr:
The 17th edition of the IDEF once again demonstrated that the Turkish defence and aerospace industry has reached a globally competitive level. Reflecting the industry’s current standing, this year’s event was marked by major contracts focusing on platform exports. The export contracts signed for the KAAN National Combat Aircraft (MMU) and the HÜRJET jet trainer aircraft suggest that, following its achievements in unmanned aerial vehicles, Türkiye is now poised to become a globally influential actor in manned platforms as well. The contract signed for the İstif-class frigate enabled the industry to advance into exporting frigate-class vessels as well, following its earlier corvette exports. MSI Turkish Defence Review (TDR) followed all key developments at the exhibition, from its opening hours to the closing moments, with an extensive team on site. In this issue, we present to our readers the first part of our IDEF 2025 Special File, prepared based on the information compiled from the exhibition. The highlights of the participating companies’ activities will be addressed in the upcoming instalments of our special file series.

 

This year, IDEF 2025, held with a new organiser and at a new exhibition venue, hosted more than 900 domestic and over 400 foreign companies from 49 different countries. In total, 1,491 exhibitors presented their products and services during the event. The exhibition, held in Istanbul from July 22 to 27, was notably attended by officials and delegations from friendly and allied nations. The exhibition hosted 231 official delegations from 114 countries. A total of 971 delegates took part in the event. With over 120,000 visitors, IDEF 2025 featured more than 1,100 products that were presented for the first time. A total of 6,301 scheduled meetings took place during the exhibition. In addition, 270 contracts and cooperation agreements were signed. As part of these agreements, a contract volume of approximately nine billion US dollars was reached. 65 percent of this total consisted of export-oriented contracts. Thus, IDEF 2025 can be considered a key contributor to the Turkish defence and aerospace industry's efforts to meet its export objectives....

contents.title_tr: ASELSAN Continues Its Growth with Double-Digit Increases in Revenue and Contracts (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: ASELSAN Continues Its Growth with Double-Digit Increases in Revenue and Contracts
contents.summary_tr: According to ASELSAN’s financial results for the first half of 2025, the company achieved a real-term revenue growth of 11.3 percent compared to the same period of the previous year, reaching ₺53.7 billion. In terms of newly signed…
contents.body_tr:
According to ASELSAN’s financial results for the first half of 2025, the company achieved a real-term revenue growth of 11.3 percent compared to the same period of the previous year, reaching ₺53.7 billion. In terms of newly signed contracts, the total value reached $2.8 billion, representing a 10 percent increase year-on-year.

ASELSAN announced its inflation-adjusted financial results for the first half of 2025 on August 5. According to the disclosure made on the Public Disclosure Platform (KAP), the company recorded notable increases in both revenue and total contract value during the first six months of the year compared to the same period in 2024. ASELSAN’s revenue rose by 11.3 percent in real terms to ₺53.7 billion, while the value of newly signed contracts increased by 10 percent, reaching $2.8 billion. This growth in revenue was driven primarily by deliveries in air defence, electronic warfare, electro-optics, radar, avionics, security, and weapon systems.

In 2025, ASELSAN signed export contracts totalling $1.3 billion, both directly and through subcontracting. Meanwhile, the company’s backlog reached $16 billion, marking a 30 percent increase over the same period last year. During this period, ASELSAN continued to invest steadily in strengthening its serial production infrastructure and in R&D activities.

ASELSAN’s performance figures for the first half of the year are as follows:

●Newly Signed Contracts: $2.8 billion

● Export Contracts: $1.3 billion

● Backlog: $16 billion

● Revenue: ₺53.7 billion

● EBITDA Margin: 25 percent

● Book-to-Bill Ratio: 2

● Net Debt/EBITDA: 0.57

● R&D Expenditures: $572 million

● Infrastructure Investment Expenditures: $104 million (100 percent increase)

The company’s EBITDA margin for the six-month period increased by 100 basis points compared to the same period last year, reaching 25 percent. EBITDA itself rose by 15 percent in real terms, amounting to ₺13.5 billion. ASELSAN succeeded in maintaining a book-to-bill ratio of 2 for two consecutive years and continued this momentum into the first half of 2025, remaining above the sector average.

ASELSAN increased its R&D expenditures by 42 percent compared to the previous year, reaching $572 million. The company also doubled its investments in serial production infrastructure over the same period, surpassing $100 million.

 

ASELSAN Further Improves Debt Metrics and Financial Discipline in H1 2025

In the first half of 2025, the share of financial liabilities in ASELSAN’s total assets decreased to 12.7 percent, down from 14.5 percent in the same period of 2024. Commercial debts also declined by 21 percent compared to the end of 2024. Year-on-year, net debt was reduced by 38 percent. As a result, ASELSAN’s Net Debt/EBITDA ratio dropped from 1.21 in the first half of 2024 to 0.57 in the current reporting period. The company also recorded improvements in cash flow. During the period, operating cash flow (OCF) stood at ₺13.6 billion, while free cash flow (FCF) remained positive at ₺816 million.

Commenting on ASELSAN’s H1 2025 financial results, Ahmet Akyol, General Manager of ASELSAN, noted that the aselsaneXt programme, which was launched in 2024, had created strong financial momentum that continued into the first half of 2025. He stated: “Three key elements have contributed to this success: a focus on higher-technology products with shorter development cycles, enhanced efficiency, and our indigenisation efforts. We are increasing the share of revenue from newly developed products. For instance, in the first half of this year, we delivered eight new products to inventory for the first time. Through the integration of artificial intelligence into our processes, we achieved annual savings of $25 million. Despite a significant rise in our workforce, we improved our revenue per employee by 1.6 percent. Moreover, orders placed for products we indigenised together with our suppliers have created substantial cost advantages. These achievements confirm that ASELSAN possesses not only the capacity to finance its present but also the discipline to secure its future.”

Akyol emphasised that the first half of 2025 was not only productive in terms of financial performance but also marked by strategic milestones: “During the IDEF exhibition, we showcased 10 new products featuring high technology and significant added value. Among these were EJDERHA, our airborne electromagnetic shield that will be a critical component of the Steel Dome system; GÖKTAN, which will redefine land-to-land strike capabilities; and ASELFLIR-600, currently the best in its class worldwide. These systems drew strong interest from international visitors. This positive outlook is the result of our technological competence, financial performance, and the influence of recent global developments.”

Highlighting ASELSAN’s strategic direction for the remainder of the year, Akyol added: “We will continue expanding our serial production capabilities in critical areas such as air defence, radar, smart munitions, guidance systems and electro-optics. Our export-oriented growth strategy will open new markets. With increasing global security demands and evolving geopolitical dynamics, the defence industry is poised for faster growth. Countries are significantly raising their defence budgets. Leveraging our engineering strength and strategic foresight, we aim to drive strong, sustainable growth both domestically and internationally, through technologies that will shape the future battlefield.”

 

Contracts Signed by ASELSAN in the First Half of 2025

● Export contract signed with an international customer for military communication systems

● Export contract signed with an international customer for radar, weapon, air defence, and datalink systems for naval platforms

● Export contract signed with an international customer for airborne electro-optical payloads

● Export contract signed for the supply of electronic warfare, communication, radar, electro-optical, and remote-controlled weapon systems for international customers

● Procurement contract signed with the Secretariat of Defence Industries for next-generation radar systems

● Procurement contract signed with the Secretariat of Defence Industries for Public Safety Communication Systems

● Procurement contract signed with Türkiye Rail System Vehicles Industry Inc. (TÜRASAŞ) for railway signalling systems

● Procurement contract signed with a domestic customer for land platform payloads

● Procurement contract signed with an international customer for radar, weapon, air defence, and datalink systems for naval platforms

● Procurement contract signed with an international customer for military communication systems

● Procurement contract signed with an international customer for guidance kits and communication systems

● Procurement contract signed with Türkiye Rail System Vehicles Industry Inc. (TÜRASAŞ) for subsystems to be used in high-speed trains

● Procurement contract signed with BMC Defence Industry and Trade Inc. for land platform payloads

contents.title_tr: Prof. Dr. Görgün: “We are now exporting trust, not just products.” (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Prof. Dr. Görgün: “We are now exporting trust, not just products.”
contents.summary_tr: The Secretariat of Defence Industries held the “Export Consultation Meeting” with broad participation from industry representatives. Held on August 26, the meeting placed particular emphasis on consultation, strategy, and synergy, in…
contents.body_tr:
The Secretariat of Defence Industries held the “Export Consultation Meeting” with broad participation from industry representatives. Held on August 26, the meeting placed particular emphasis on consultation, strategy, and synergy, in line with the global vision of Türkiye’s defence and aerospace industry.

Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of Defence Industries, drew attention to the export performance achieved by the sector during his post-event remarks. He underlined that Türkiye’s defence and aerospace industry demonstrates not only commercial success, but also a strategic vision.

According to the data shared by Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün:

● The sector has exported to 185 countries to date,

● A total of 230 different products has been delivered abroad,

● In 2024, annual exports reached $7.1 billion,

● In the first seven months of this year, exports totalled $4.591 billion, marking a 38.6 percent increase.

Prof. Dr. Görgün stated that this picture reflects the outcome of indigenous engineering, the efforts in the field, and the sector’s shared vision. He added: “We are now exporting trust, not just products.”

contents.title_tr: ASELSAN Lays the Foundations for the Next 50 Years (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: ASELSAN Lays the Foundations for the Next 50 Years
contents.summary_tr: As part of its initiative titled Laying the Foundations for the Next 50 Years, ASELSAN held a ceremony on August 27 at its Gölbaşı campus, which featured Steel Dome Deliveries, Facility Inaugurations, and the Groundbreaking of the…
contents.body_tr:
As part of its initiative titled Laying the Foundations for the Next 50 Years, ASELSAN held a ceremony on August 27 at its Gölbaşı campus, which featured Steel Dome Deliveries, Facility Inaugurations, and the Groundbreaking of the Oğulbey Technology Base. The event was attended by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

During the event, components of the Steel Dome, comprising 47 platforms and valued at more than $460 million, were formally delivered. These included systems such as the HİSAR O+ and SİPER air defence systems; ALP 300-G and 100-G radars; PUHU 3-LT and REDET electronic warfare systems; and the KORKUT 150/35 and 130/35 air defence vehicles.

Also inaugurated during the ceremony were 14 new facilities constructed as part of a $280 million investment. Covering an area of 165,000 square metres, these facilities are expected to increase ASELSAN’s production capacity by 40 percent. Along with providing employment for an additional 4,000 personnel, the facilities feature 23,000 square metres of cleanroom and laboratory infrastructure to support advanced testing and integration processes.

The ceremony also marked the groundbreaking of ASELSAN’s Oğulbey Technology Base, a project valued at $1.5 billion. Described as the largest single investment in the history of the Republic of Türkiye’s defence and aerospace sector, the base will serve as a hub for the development of quantum and AI-driven defence algorithms, as well as future communication and command-and-control systems.

In his speech, President Erdoğan emphasised that these three milestones would strengthen the Turkish Armed Forces and elevate the country’s defence and aerospace capabilities to a new level.

 

Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of the Defence Industries, underlined that the defence and aerospace ecosystem,  which now achieves an 83 percent domestic production rate and has surpassed USD 7.1 billion in exports to 185 countries, has evolved into a symbol of Türkiye’s strategic leadership, not only on the battlefield but also on the global stage.

contents.title_en: TETRONE BATTERIES Launches Operations
contents.summary_tr: The expertise accumulated by ASPİLSAN Enerji, which operates Türkiye’s first lithium-ion battery production facility, is now being transferred to the civilian sector through TETRONE BATTERIES. Supported by ASPİLSAN Enerji’s engineering…
contents.summary_en: The expertise accumulated by ASPİLSAN Enerji, which operates Türkiye’s first lithium-ion battery production facility, is now being transferred to the civilian sector through TETRONE BATTERIES. Supported by ASPİLSAN Enerji’s engineering capabilities and production infrastructure, the TETRONE BATTERIES brand has officially launched operations to deliver tailored mobile energy solutions for individual and corporate users.
contents.body_tr:
The expertise accumulated by ASPİLSAN Enerji, which operates Türkiye’s first lithium-ion battery production facility, is now being transferred to the civilian sector through TETRONE BATTERIES. Supported by ASPİLSAN Enerji’s engineering capabilities and production infrastructure, the TETRONE BATTERIES brand has officially launched operations to deliver tailored mobile energy solutions for individual and corporate users.

In a statement made on August 8, Prof. Dr. Ahmet Turan Özdemir, General Manager of ASPİLSAN Enerji, said, “With TETRONE BATTERIES, we aim to enhance perceptions of quality in the civilian market and contribute to everyday life.”

Offering battery sales, replacement, and technical support services for a wide range of products—primarily consumer electronics and robotic systems—TETRONE BATTERIES provides solutions for various systems, from electric bicycles to medical devices. The brand operates through an e-commerce infrastructure and is accessible across Türkiye via www.tetrone.com.tr.

contents.body_tr:

Over the past eight years, CANiK pistols have received the “Handgun of the Year” award on multiple occasions, across various categories of the competition.

Cahit Utku Aral, General Manager, SYS Group, stated on August 8 that this success marks a significant development expected to boost sales in both the US and international markets.

contents.title_en: TCG VOLKAN Begins Service in the Maldives Under Its New Name
contents.summary_tr: TCG VOLKAN (P-343), donated by Türkiye, was formally commissioned into the inventory of the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF). The vessel will serve in the Maldivian Navy under the name DHARUMAVANTHA.
contents.summary_en: TCG VOLKAN (P-343), donated by Türkiye, was formally commissioned into the inventory of the Maldives National Defence Force (MNDF). The vessel will serve in the Maldivian Navy under the name DHARUMAVANTHA.
contents.body_tr:
The commissioning ceremony of TCG VOLKAN was held on August 15 with the participation of the President of the Republic of Maldives Dr. Mohamed Muizzu, senior state officials of the country, Semih Lütfü Turgut, Ambassador of Türkiye to Colombo, and Admiral Kadir Yıldız, Commander of the Fleet Command.

As part of the defence industry cooperation, the transfer of TCG VOLKAN began on July 1 and was successfully completed on August 7. On August 10, following the vessel’s berthing at Malé Port, a Turkish flag-lowering ceremony was held. The ceremony was also attended by the Military Attaché accredited to the Maldives, based in New Delhi, and the Director General for International Defence Cooperation and Policy at the Maldives National Defence Force.

contents.title_en: Bayraktar AKINCI Hits Targets with ALPAGUT and EREN
contents.summary_tr: During a test conducted with the integration of the Bayraktar AKINCI Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle (UCAV), the ALPAGUT Loitering Munition System and the EREN missile equipped with an electro-optical seeker successfully struck their…
contents.summary_en: During a test conducted with the integration of the Bayraktar AKINCI Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle (UCAV), the ALPAGUT Loitering Munition System and the EREN missile equipped with an electro-optical seeker successfully struck their designated targets.
contents.body_tr:
The test was carried out off the coast of Sinop, featuring the ALPAGUT Loitering Munition System, which is developed jointly by STM and Roketsan, together with the EREN missile, also developed by Roketsan, which is designed for launch from multiple platforms.

Released from Bayraktar AKINCI, ALPAGUT loitered in the air for a designated period to detect and assess the target. Once the target was identified, it executed a dive and launched the turbojet-powered EREN missile, which is equipped with artificial intelligence capabilities, completing the mission successfully.

Previously, ALPAGUT had demonstrated precision strike capability in ground-launch tests. With this latest test, it also validated its performance in safe aerial release, wing deployment, navigation, and optical guidance.

On August 7, Özgür Güleryüz, General Manager of STM, commented: “The ALPAGUT Loitering Munition System, which we developed in cooperation with Roketsan, has successfully completed its flight test with the Bayraktar AKINCI UCAV. With an operational radius of 60 kilometres, an endurance of over 60 minutes, and the ability to operate both day and night, ALPAGUT will serve as an effective asset against both stationary and mobile land or sea targets.”

contents.title_tr: MİDLAS Launches HİSAR-D RF Against Naval Target (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: MİDLAS Launches HİSAR-D RF Against Naval Target
contents.summary_tr: The National Vertical Launching System (MİDLAS), developed by Roketsan, successfully launched the HİSAR-D RF missile, produced by ASELSAN, during its latest firing test conducted from TCG İSTANBUL (F-515).
contents.summary_en: The National Vertical Launching System (MİDLAS), developed by Roketsan, successfully launched the HİSAR-D RF missile, produced by ASELSAN, during its latest firing test conducted from TCG İSTANBUL (F-515).
contents.body_tr:
The first firing test of MİDLAS was carried out on a land-based platform in 2022, followed by a second test from TCG İSTANBUL in 2024. In the most recent trial, conducted off the coast of Sinop against a naval target, the CENK 400-N AESA 4D search radar was used to detect the target, while engagement was achieved using the AKREP 300-N fire control radar.

The successful interception was made possible by the integration of ASELSAN’s HİSAR-D fire control system, GÜDÜ 200-MG ship-based data link unit, onboard data link, CENK 400-N AESA 4D search radar, AKREP 300-N fire control radar, and AGRAS 2203/SA seeker head for naval targets.

On August 15, Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of the Defence Industries, issued a statement emphasising that the successful repetition of the test reinforced the systems’ reliability and underlined the collaborative spirit within the defence and aerospace sector. Prof. Dr. Görgün commended the synergy generated by the teams working shoulder to shoulder, from ASELSAN to HAVELSAN, STM to Roketsan, and highlighted the added value this collective effort has brought to the Turkish Naval Forces, extending his congratulations to all engineers and personnel involved.

contents.title_tr: MKE’s Contribution to ALTAY’s Striking Power (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: MKE’s Contribution to ALTAY’s Striking Power
contents.summary_tr: Within the scope of the ALTAY Main Battle Tank Production Program, the Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) will manufacture a total of 250 weapon systems in the upcoming phase.
contents.summary_en: Within the scope of the ALTAY Main Battle Tank Production Program, the Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) will manufacture a total of 250 weapon systems in the upcoming phase.
contents.body_tr:
Under the ALTAY main battle tank project coordinated by the Secretariat of Defence Industries (SSB), MKE is manufacturing the 120 mm 55-calibre main gun system and the 7.62 mm PMT-76/57A platform machine gun, both of which are integrated into the tanks.

Having successfully delivered various weapon systems to the main contractor BMC to date, MKE continues its efforts for the upcoming period. In a statement made by MKE officials on August 28, it was stated that, in addition to the target of manufacturing 250 weapon systems, the company is also planning to assume responsibility for technical support, logistics services and training activities related to these systems.

The 120 mm 55-calibre main gun system produced by MKE is distinguished by its compatibility with NATO-standard STANAG 4385 ammunition. As a smoothbore gun system, it features a hard chrome-plated barrel measuring 6,600 mm in length. With a rate of fire of 6 rounds per minute, the system offers an effective range of at least 2,000 metres with chemical energy ammunition and at least 3,000 metres with kinetic energy armour-piercing rounds.

Coaxially mounted to the main gun of the ALTAY tank, the PMT-76/57A is an indigenous design developed by MKE and is named after the legendary 57th Infantry Regiment, which fought heroically at Çanakkale (Gallipoli). The weapon uses 7.62x51 mm NATO-standard ammunition, has a minimum rate of fire of 600 rounds per minute, and weighs 12 kilograms.

contents.title_tr: HAVELSAN Delivers 60th GVDS to the 8th Ship of the MİLGEM Project (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: HAVELSAN Delivers 60th GVDS to the 8th Ship of the MİLGEM Project
contents.summary_tr: HAVELSAN successfully completed the 60th delivery of its Ship Data Distribution System (GVDS), developed for submarines and surface vessels. The system passed factory acceptance tests with an A grade, and was delivered for integration…
contents.summary_en: HAVELSAN successfully completed the 60th delivery of its Ship Data Distribution System (GVDS), developed for submarines and surface vessels. The system passed factory acceptance tests with an A grade, and was delivered for integration into the eighth ship of the MİLGEM project.
contents.body_tr:
Also referred to as the Submarine Data Distribution System (DBDS) in submarines, the system ensures high-performance data flow and system integration even under the most challenging conditions. Through subsystems such as the Single Board Computer (SBC), interface cards, time card, power and backplane semi-finished cards, time server, and GNSS unit, HAVELSAN has raised the indigenous contribution rate of the GVDS and DBDS product family to over 80 percent.

HAVELSAN first delivered the GVDS fifteen years ago for the TCG HEYBELİADA (F-511). Operating on a 24/7 basis aboard all ships and submarines, the system has now surpassed a cumulative total of 300 years in operational use.

contents.title_tr: Definition of SMEs Revised, Enabling More Companies to Benefit from State Support Mechanisms (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Definition of SMEs Revised, Enabling More Companies to Benefit from State Support Mechanisms
contents.summary_tr: With a presidential decree, companies with a net turnover or financial balance sheet not exceeding ₺1,000,000,000 have been included within the scope of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs).
contents.summary_en: With a presidential decree, companies with a net turnover or financial balance sheet not exceeding ₺1,000,000,000 have been included within the scope of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs).
contents.body_tr:
The Presidential Decree No. 10182, published on August 7, introduced a revision to the definition of SMEs (Small and Medium-sized Enterprises). As a result of the regulation published in the Official Gazette, a significant number of companies that were previously excluded from SME status solely due to their annual turnover can now be classified as SMEs.

Prior to the amendment, SMEs were defined as enterprises with fewer than 250 employees and with either an annual net turnover or financial balance sheet not exceeding ₺500,000,000. The revised regulation raised this threshold to ₺1,000,000,000. Accordingly, companies that still employ fewer than 250 personnel, and whose net turnover or financial balance sheet remains below ₺1,000,000,000, are now eligible for SME classification.

This redefinition enables such companies to access state support mechanisms provided by institutions such as the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Organisation (KOSGEB) and the Technology and Innovation Funding Programmes Directorate of TÜBİTAK (TEYDEB).

contents.title_tr: Turkish Defence and Aerospace Sector Achieves 128 Percent Export Growth in July (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Turkish Defence and Aerospace Sector Achieves 128 Percent Export Growth in July
contents.summary_tr: Türkiye’s defence and aerospace sector increased its exports by 128.4 percent in July 2025 compared to the same month of the previous year, reaching $989.6 million. Cumulative exports for the January–July period totalled $4.591 billion…
contents.summary_en: Türkiye’s defence and aerospace sector increased its exports by 128.4 percent in July 2025 compared to the same month of the previous year, reaching $989.6 million. Cumulative exports for the January–July period totalled $4.591 billion, reflecting a 38.6 percent year-on-year increase.
contents.body_tr:
Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of the Defence Industries, shared the export figures with the public on August 2. Emphasising that this achievement is the result of sustainable production and export policies, Prof. Dr. Görgün noted that the increase underscores the effectiveness of strategies based on product diversity, platform-centric solutions and the export of complete systems.

“We continue to strengthen our presence in global markets through high local content solutions, under the leadership of our President,” said Prof. Dr. Görgün, who highlighted the integrated structure of the sector—from main contractors to SMEs—as the cornerstone of the export ecosystem. He also extended his appreciation to all companies and teams involved for their contributions.

contents.title_tr: Six Defence and Aerospace Companies Among the Fastest-Growing 100 (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Six Defence and Aerospace Companies Among the Fastest-Growing 100
contents.summary_tr: IDAK Aviation, TUALCOM, CNK Aerostructural Assembly, CNK Aerospace, INFINIA and Koluman Otomotiv, six companies operating in the defence and aerospace industry, were included in the list of the fastest-growing 100 companies…
contents.body_tr:
IDAK Aviation, TUALCOM, CNK Aerostructural Assembly, CNK Aerospace, INFINIA and Koluman Otomotiv, six companies operating in the defence and aerospace industry, were included in the list of the fastest-growing 100 companies, representing the sector with distinction.

The Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (TOBB), in cooperation with The Economic Policy Research Foundation of Türkiye (TEPAV) and TOBB University of Economics and Technology (TOBB ETÜ), has announced the 100 fastest-growing companies in Türkiye. The evaluation was based on companies’ annual revenue growth between 2021 and 2023. Defence and aerospace firms secured high rankings on the list, reflecting the sector’s dynamic performance.

The rankings of the sector’s companies based on their growth rates are as follows:

● IDAK Aviation ranked 9th with 3,481 percent growth

● TUALCOM ranked 17th with 2,094 percent growth

● CNK Aerostructural Assembly ranked 20th with 1,849 percent growth

● INFINIA ranked 33rd with 1,210 percent growth

● CNK Aerospace ranked 80th with 678 percent growth

● Koluman Otomotiv ranked 91st with 623 percent growth

contents.summary_tr: The ammunition production line established by the Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) in Mongolia is now ready for operation following the completion of final preparations. In a statement made by MKE officials on September 13, it was…
contents.body_tr:
The ammunition production line established by the Mechanical and Chemical Industry (MKE) in Mongolia is now ready for operation following the completion of final preparations. In a statement made by MKE officials on September 13, it was announced that the project to establish the ammunition production line, initiated under the contract signed between MKE and Mongolia’s Defence Industrial Corporation (DIC), had been successfully completed.

The installation of machinery and equipment, commissioning, performance testing and pilot batch production phases were all finalised, and the line was officially accepted. The facility will now begin manufacturing ammunition in 9x18 mm, 7.62x54 mm and 7.62x39 mm calibres.

contents.title_tr: KEYVAN Aviation and Quantum3D Sign MoU for Global Collaboration (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: KEYVAN Aviation and Quantum3D Sign MoU for Global Collaboration
contents.summary_tr: KEYVAN Aviation signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Quantum3D, a company based in Silicon Valley, to initiate a strategic collaboration. Under this agreement, the two companies will pursue global-scale joint projects aimed…
contents.body_tr:
KEYVAN Aviation signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Quantum3D, a company based in Silicon Valley, to initiate a strategic collaboration. Under this agreement, the two companies will pursue global-scale joint projects aimed at generating new value for airlines, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), training centres, and next-generation mobility programmes.

According to a statement released by KEYVAN Aviation on September 8, the cooperation will see KEYVAN Aviation provide certified aviation data sets, charts, and intelligence for operational domains. Quantum3D will contribute its MANTIS image generation and sensor simulation software, along with its Independence IDX hardware platforms. Through this partnership, the companies will develop integrated solutions in the aviation field.

Mehmet Keyvan, CEO of KEYVAN Aviation, stated that the collaboration presents new opportunities for customers. Murat Köse, CEO of Quantum3D, noted that the agreement is expected to contribute to the future of aviation and Urban/Advanced Air Mobility (UAM/AAM).

contents.title_tr: Turkish Air Force Expands Its T-70 Helicopter Fleet (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Turkish Air Force Expands Its T-70 Helicopter Fleet
contents.summary_tr: The Turkish Air Force has added its fourth T-70 utility helicopter to its inventory. The Air Force had previously received its third T-70 during a handover ceremony held in August 2024. With this latest addition, the service has taken…
contents.body_tr:
The Turkish Air Force has added its fourth T-70 utility helicopter to its inventory. The Air Force had previously received its third T-70 during a handover ceremony held in August 2024. With this latest addition, the service has taken delivery of its fourth T-70 after a hiatus of nearly one year. The Ministry of National Defence announced on September 4 that inspection and acceptance procedures for the helicopter had been completed and that the platform had officially entered into service.

T-70 helicopters are among the key aerial assets that enhance the operational capabilities of the Turkish Armed Forces. Based on Sikorsky’s UH-60 Black Hawk platform, the T-70 is produced under licence by Turkish Aerospace. The platform delivers high performance in high-altitude, hot-weather, and rugged terrain conditions. The T-70 is suited for a wide range of missions, including medical evacuation, cargo transport, search and rescue, and special operations.

contents.title_tr: HAVELSAN to Establish the B-250 Simulation and Training Ecosystem (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: HAVELSAN to Establish the B-250 Simulation and Training Ecosystem
contents.summary_tr: HAVELSAN will develop simulation and training technologies for pilots operating the B-250 light attack and trainer aircraft, manufactured by CALIDUS. In a statement released on September 3, HAVELSAN officials provided details about the…
contents.body_tr:
HAVELSAN will develop simulation and training technologies for pilots operating the B-250 light attack and trainer aircraft, manufactured by CALIDUS. In a statement released on September 3, HAVELSAN officials provided details about the training ecosystem to be developed. Under the agreement, a high-fidelity simulator infrastructure will be established to ensure comprehensive pre-mission preparation on the ground for real-life operations. These systems will be installed at CALIDUS’ facilities in the United Arab Emirates.

Signed during IDEF 2025, the agreement is considered significant not only for the delivery of the systems, but also as a testament to the two companies shared commitment to innovation, security, and long-term cooperation.

The Ecosystem Integrates Theoretical Knowledge and Practical Readiness

The flight training simulator included in HAVELSAN’s package features a simulation system that replicates real mission scenarios with advanced flight dynamics. The partial mission simulators comprise training modules focused on mission-critical manoeuvres and subsystems. The cockpit ingress/egress simulator offers safety-oriented instruction for emergency evacuation procedures. The briefing/debriefing station functions as an interactive platform for mission planning, analysis, and performance evaluation.

Dr. Mehmet Akif Nacar, General Manager, HAVELSAN, emphasised that their simulation solutions are designed not only to mirror real-world conditions, but also to build pilot readiness for unforeseen scenarios. Dr. Mehmet Akif Nacar, General Manager, HAVELSAN, added: “This project with CALIDUS is a strong reflection of our vision to develop human-centric, integrated and reliable systems.” Dr. Khalifa Murad Al Balooshi, Managing Director and CEO, CALIDUS, emphasised that the cooperation represents a long-term strategic partnership built on trust and innovation. He stated: “Our decision to rely on HAVELSAN’s expertise in training will provide B-250 users with advanced, technology-driven capabilities that are fit for the future.”

contents.title_tr: Serpil Gönenç Dinçer Appointed as General Manager of Nurol Teknoloji (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Serpil Gönenç Dinçer Appointed as General Manager of Nurol Teknoloji
contents.summary_tr: Selim Baybaş, General Manager of Nurol Teknoloji, has handed over his position to Deputy General Manager Serpil Gönenç Dinçer. With this appointment, Dinçer has become the first woman to serve as General Manager since the company’s…
contents.body_tr:
Selim Baybaş, General Manager of Nurol Teknoloji, has handed over his position to Deputy General Manager Serpil Gönenç Dinçer. With this appointment, Dinçer has become the first woman to serve as General Manager since the company’s establishment.

Baybaş announced the transition on August 31, stating: "Today marks a special day for me. I take great pride and joy in transferring the role of General Manager of Nurol Teknoloji, which I have held for nearly six years, to my esteemed colleague and fellow companion on this journey, Ms. Dinçer. During this time, we served not only our national security forces but also the armed forces of friendly and allied nations. The products we developed, using entirely indigenous resources, have reached the capacity to protect over a million personnel, hundreds of land platforms, and numerous naval and aerial systems.

The past six years were marked by dozens of patents, the establishment of international subsidiaries, acquisitions, strategic partnerships, major joint ventures, hundreds of millions of dollars in defence exports, and robust investments. These achievements were made possible thanks to our dedicated and hard-working team members, who embody the highest values. Knowing each of you has been a privilege. I extend my heartfelt thanks for making these six years unforgettable.

I have full confidence that, under the leadership of Ms. Dinçer, who will be our Group’s first woman General Manager, Nurol Teknoloji will achieve even greater success, not only in Türkiye but on a global scale. I will follow Nurol Teknoloji’s achievements with pride and happiness. The journey continues."

 

Dinçer holds a bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering from Middle East Technical University (METU), and a master's degree in Systems Management from METU’s Industrial Engineering Department. She later completed executive MBA programmes at the University of Michigan and Bilkent University. With 21 years of experience in the defence and aerospace sectors, Dinçer has also held roles at Roketsan and ASELSAN.

MSI Turkish Defence Review extends its best wishes to Serpil Gönenç Dinçer in her new role.

contents.title_tr: İÇEL, 4th of İ Class Frigates, Launched (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: İÇEL, 4th of İ Class Frigates, Launched
contents.summary_tr: İÇEL (F-518), the eighth vessel of the MİLGEM project and 4 th of İ class frigates, was launched at a ceremony held at Sefine Shipyard. Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of the Defence Industries, announced the development with the…
contents.body_tr:
İÇEL (F-518), the eighth vessel of the MİLGEM project and 4th of İ class frigates, was launched at a ceremony held at Sefine Shipyard. Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün, Secretary of the Defence Industries, announced the development with the words: “A milestone has been passed in the MİLGEM project.”

On September 1, Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün shared details about the construction process of the frigate İÇEL. He stated: “This vessel, imbued with the spirit of independence in every steel plate and the will of engineering in every weld, is more than just a platform. It is a strategic signature etched into our seas. Following the enthusiasm of the recently completed Blue Homeland TEKNOFEST, the launch of our İÇEL frigate further reinforces both our deterrence at sea and our strategic resolve. Every new vessel rising on the vast horizons of the Blue Homeland demonstrates our security capacity as well as our engineering prowess and unyielding commitment to sovereignty in full view of the world.”

Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün noted that over 200 institutions and companies have taken part in the project under the coordination of the Secretariat of Defence Industries, and continued: “This accomplishment strengthens our Navy and contributes to the broader defence industry ecosystem. Türkiye, now among the nations with the highest number of concurrent military shipbuilding programmes, is asserting itself not just at sea, but as a decisive actor in the strategic landscape of the global defence industry.”

With a length of 113 metres and a displacement of 3,200 tonnes, İÇEL was constructed with an indigenisation rate of up to 80 percent. The vessel is equipped to carry out multi-role missions, including reconnaissance, surveillance, anti-submarine and air defence operations, as well as search and rescue tasks. In the coming period, the ship will also be integrated with the ATMACA anti-ship missile, the MİDLAS vertical launch system, the GÖKDENİZ close-in weapon system, the ADVENT combat management system, and the CENK 3D search radar.

contents.title_tr: New ALTAY Tanks Delivered to the Turkish Armed Forces (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: New ALTAY Tanks Delivered to the Turkish Armed Forces
contents.summary_tr: As part of the ALTAY Main Battle Tank Project, the Turkish Armed Forces (TAF) has added three new ALTAY tanks to its inventory to meet its main battle tank requirements. The tanks were officially delivered during the inauguration…
contents.body_tr:
As part of the ALTAY Main Battle Tank Project, the Turkish Armed Forces (TAF) has added three new ALTAY tanks to its inventory to meet its main battle tank requirements. The tanks were officially delivered during the inauguration ceremony of the BMC Ankara Tank and Next-Generation Vehicles Production Facility. With this latest delivery, the number of new ALTAY tanks in the TAF inventory has increased to five. The facility is set to begin serial production of the tanks in the upcoming period.

The ceremony held on October 28 was attended by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan; Minister of National Defence Yaşar Güler; Minister of Foreign Affairs Hakan Fidan; Minister of Agriculture and Forestry İbrahim Yumaklı; Minister of Industry and Technology Fatih Mehmet Kacır; Minister of Family and Social Services Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş; Minister of Youth and Sports Osman Aşkın Bak; Secretary of the Defence Industries Prof. Dr. Haluk Görgün; Chief of the General Staff General Selçuk Bayraktaroğlu; and Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman bin Hassan bin Ali Al Thani, along with numerous military and civilian guests....

contents.title_tr: New Phase in the National Fast Attack Craft Project: First Hull Block Transferred to Slipway (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: New Phase in the National Fast Attack Craft Project: First Hull Block Transferred to Slipway
contents.summary_tr: The first hull block constructed under the National Fast Attack Craft Project, designed and contracted by STM, has been transferred to the slipway. A ceremony was held at Istanbul Shipyard on October 27 to mark the milestone. During the…
contents.body_tr:
The first hull block constructed under the National Fast Attack Craft Project, designed and contracted by STM, has been transferred to the slipway. A ceremony was held at Istanbul Shipyard on October 27 to mark the milestone. During the ceremony, Özgür Güleryüz, General Manager of STM, underlined that Türkiye had reached another critical milestone in its journey to achieving independent naval defence capabilities. He stated: “Following the initial steel cutting, we have now placed the first hull block of our indigenous Fast Attack Craft, entirely designed by STM engineers, onto the slipway. This project signifies the production of a new platform and marks Türkiye’s emergence as a country capable of designing and building its own fast attack craft. Distinguished by its original design, high local content, modern weapon systems, and advanced maritime capabilities, our National Fast Attack Craft will enhance deterrence in the Blue Homeland.”

A contract between the Secretariat of Defence Industries (SSB) and STM for the National Fast Attack Craft Project was signed on September 9, 2024. The first steel cutting took place on July 8, 2025. STM continues to pursue its construction activities with a focus on maximising local content in both design and production phases....

contents.title_tr: Smart Drone Station KORGAN-M Poised to Become the Brain of Field Operations (MSI TDR)
contents.title_en: Smart Drone Station KORGAN-M Poised to Become the Brain of Field Operations
contents.summary_tr: Developed by SAVX Teknoloji, the smart drone station KORGAN-M is now ready for deployment in the field. KORGAN-M can autonomously deploy unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) across different areas and initiate missions with a single command…
contents.body_tr:
Developed by SAVX Teknoloji, the smart drone station KORGAN-M is now ready for deployment in the field. KORGAN-M can autonomously deploy unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) across different areas and initiate missions with a single command, without the need for an operator.

In a statement issued on October 17, representatives of Pasifik Teknoloji highlighted that KORGAN-M, a new product by its affiliate SAVX Teknoloji, is capable of operating in electronic warfare environments without relying on GPS connectivity. The remotely controllable station also integrates seamlessly with the Seyyah Visual Navigation System, developed entirely by TİTRA Teknoloji, to deliver real-time intelligence. Once deployed, the system remains on standby 24/7 and enables cloud-based mission planning, real-time monitoring, and AI-assisted data analytics, accelerating decision-making processes. KORGAN-M has been engineered to operate continuously under adverse weather conditions....
